summary: Publisher Data S1D and the registered SPIP-minus-LPIP analysis share 13,311 uniquely paired genes. Pearson is 0.95202, Spearman is 0.89977 and 11,520 pairs (86.54%) agree in direction, so neither numerical route meets author-concordance-v2. The registered fit also retains SPIP19, which the authors excluded.

manualReview.summary: Published Data S1D compared with registered photoperiod effects for 13,311 genes
manualReview.note: The registered SPIP-minus-LPIP contrast includes SPIP19 (GSM6199271). The archived author script excludes this library for poor sequencing quality. GEO and the script give six LP and five LPIP after exclusion, while STAR Methods gives five LP and six LPIP. Sheet D reports LPIP minus SPIP, as confirmed by the two LP-referenced coefficients in sheet A. The archived four-group edgeR script omits the sheet-D contrast command. The comparison uses the reported D effects, raw P values and FDRs. Applying the script’s median CPM ≥ 1 rule to the 20 retained GEO libraries recovers all 13,345 D identifiers. STAR Methods also describes a 10-raw-count cutoff and gives 13,346 genes. At FDR < 0.05 the full author table has 497 calls and the public registered table has 333, with 301 in common among unique pairs.
reviewFlags: The registered fit retains SPIP19. The authors excluded it for poor sequencing quality.
The paper and archived design give different LP and LPIP group sizes. STAR Methods reports 13,346 retained genes, while the implemented filter and Data S1D give 13,345.
Spearman is 0.89977248 and same-gene direction agreement is 0.86544963. Coverage and Pearson meet their v2 thresholds.

verificationReview.reason: Data S1D is publicly available and has been compared. Neither v2 numerical route passes. The authors excluded SPIP19, the registered fit retains it, and the paper reports different LP/LPIP group sizes from the archived design.
verificationReview.nextStep: For exact cohort and inference sign-off, obtain the sample-to-design map for the fitted libraries and the command that generated the sheet-D test. Keep any four-group refit or SPIP19 sensitivity analysis separate from the registered output.

comparabilityReview.basis: Compare the current registered two-arm edgeR-QL result with the full published pairwise test in Data S1D. Both effect estimates measure a log2 expression difference between the intermediate-photoperiod groups. The author analysis used a different cohort and model.
comparabilityReview.reference: Melum et al., Current Biology (2024), Data S1D and STAR Methods. Sheet A and the workbook’s sheet-D import identify the contrast. Zenodo 10285435 documents the four-group analysis and named exclusion. GEO GSE204883 supplies sample labels and count files.

cohort.note: Both analyses use P50 laser-captured hypothalamic ependymal tissue from Siberian hamsters. The script removes SPIP19 by name and assigns the remaining libraries to groups by column position. Its six LP, five LPIP, four SPIP and five SP agree with the GEO file labels after exclusion. STAR Methods reports five LP and six LPIP. The registered contrast includes all five deposited libraries from each intermediate group, including SPIP19 (GSM6199271).

contrast.note: Sheet D reports LPIP minus SPIP. Its workbook import names glm_test_LPIP_SPIP_anno_median_cpm1.txt, and its logFC equals the LP-referenced LPIP coefficient minus the LP-referenced SPIP coefficient from sheet A for all 13,345 IDs, to workbook precision. The extraction negates D once. The comparison reads SPIP_minus_LPIP with orientationSign +1. Both groups transferred to intermediate photoperiod at weaning.

features.note: Join the original mouse-projected Ensembl IDs to the registered feature map. Pair a symbol only when it has one input feature. Of 34 unpaired author rows, 23 map to aggregate symbols, 9 lack a registered symbol, and 2 map to symbols absent from the output. The 627 unpaired registered symbols comprise 22 aggregates and 605 without an author feature.

effects.note: Both analyses estimate group differences on the edgeR log2 scale. Across all 13,311 pairs, Pearson is 0.95202240 and Spearman is 0.89977248. All pairs have two nonzero effects and 11,520 agree in sign. Median absolute log2 difference is 0.05284, maximum 0.99076, and the ratio of registered to author RMS effect is 1.00590.

inference.note: The archived four-group script applies median CPM ≥ 1 before TMM and uses edgeR quasi-likelihood tests. It omits the command for D. Sheet D supplies the reported F, raw P and FDR, and BH on its 13,345 raw P values reproduces its FDRs to workbook precision. The registered two-arm fit sums mapped counts sharing a symbol, uses filterByExpr and TMM, and adjusts across 13,948 tested rows, including ten unmapped rows omitted from the public table. All paired raw P values and FDRs are finite. At FDR < 0.05, 494 author and 320 registered genes are called among pairs, with 301 in common. Another three author and 13 published registered calls lack a pair. At the paper’s FDR < 0.001, the full tables contain 114 author and 76 published registered calls, with 74 in common.

coverage.note: Sheet D contains all 13,345 IDs recovered by applying the archived script’s filter to the deposited counts after excluding SPIP19. The registered output publishes 13,938 symbols from a 13,948-row testing family. The 13,311 unique pairs cover 99.7452% of D and 95.5015% of published registered symbols. Each denominator includes all unpaired rows in its respective table.

comparabilityReview.criteria: Full-results scope describes the published pairwise table. For concordance under author-concordance-v2, require at least 30 paired effects, at least 90% coverage of the published registered output, and compatible cohort, contrast, identifiers and effect definitions. Either Pearson and Spearman must both reach 0.90, or at least 90% of nonzero pairs must agree in sign with at least 30 such pairs covering at least 90% of all pairs. Evaluate unrounded metrics across all finite one-to-one pairs. FDR < 0.05, the paper’s FDR < 0.001, and nominal P < 0.05 provide context.
comparabilityReview.conclusion: The full published contrast was compared. Spearman falls below 0.90 and 86.54% of nonzero pairs agree in direction. The SPIP19 exclusion independently prevents a cohort match. No contrast receives full verification.

additionalComparisonSpec.localMethod: edgeR-QL, registered SPIP-minus-LPIP two-arm fit including SPIP19
additionalComparisonSpec.authorMethod: Data S1D reports a pairwise edgeR result. The archived four-group workflow uses median CPM ≥ 1, TMM and quasi-likelihood fitting after excluding SPIP19. It omits the sheet-D test command.
additionalComparisonSpec.orientation: Sheet D reports LPIP minus SPIP. Its workbook import names glm_test_LPIP_SPIP_anno_median_cpm1.txt, and its logFC equals the LP-referenced LPIP coefficient minus the LP-referenced SPIP coefficient from sheet A for all 13,345 IDs, to workbook precision. The extraction negates D once. The comparison reads SPIP_minus_LPIP with orientationSign +1.
additionalComparisonSpec.note: Full Data S1D. The normalized file retains every author row, with a unique unpaired key for aggregated or unmapped features. Only one-to-one registered symbols pair. The cohorts differ. Spearman and same-gene direction agreement fall below the v2 thresholds. The paper also gives LP/LPIP group sizes that differ from the archived design.

openIssues: The paper gives five LP and six LPIP animals. The code assigns six LP and five LPIP by column position, consistent with the deposited labels. The exact sample-to-design map for Data S1D and its specific test command remain undocumented in the archived script.
SPIP19 inclusion, different filters, symbol aggregation and four-group versus two-arm fitting can each affect estimates. The direct comparison does not apportion the differences among them.
